## What this changes

<!-- One or two sentences. -->

## Type of change

- [ ] Adding a conjecture
- [ ] Correcting an existing record (statement, identifiers, tags)
- [ ] Recording a claim about a conjecture's status
- [ ] Retracting or disputing an existing claim
- [ ] Adding a canonical Lean statement
- [ ] Submitting a Lean proof
- [ ] Code, site or tooling

## If you are recording a claim

- [ ] The source link points at the specific paper, post or page, and says what I say it says.
- [ ] The `scope` is accurate. If this settles only part of the conjecture, `scope` says which part.
- [ ] The claim type is right. A rediscovered published solution is `resolved_by_prior_literature`, not `proved`.
- [ ] The evidence tier is not overstated. `published` and `community_accepted` need a named human in `reviewer`.
- [ ] `ai_assistance` is declared honestly.

## If you are submitting a proof

- [ ] I did not modify the canonical statement file. (CI rebuilds it from the base commit regardless.)
- [ ] My proof uses no `sorry`, no `native_decide`, and no custom axioms.
- [ ] I understand a green check certifies the proof against the canonical statement, not that the statement is a faithful rendering of the conjecture.

## Declarations

- [ ] Claims I touched are append-only: I have not edited or deleted an existing claim.
- [ ] Any statement text I added has a `provenance` entry naming its source and licence.
- [ ] AI assistance used in preparing this pull request: <!-- none / which system, and for what -->
